02 / EXPERIMENT DESIGN

Experiment comparison

The original reference runs are marked. Supplementary runs complete the same-input comparison.

The stratified sample is balanced across three rating classes (50 / 50 / 50). Binary scoring merges 3-star reviews with negatives, producing 50 positives and 100 negatives. Each run uses its own rating mapping and majority baseline.

Prediction changes by sample

Same reviews, independent predictions

Rows are binary predictions; columns are three-class predictions. These are transitions between predictions, not a confusion matrix against ratings. Prompts and settings are frozen; requests share no answers or conversation. Calls were made at different times against the same named model, so this is a controlled descriptive comparison, not proof of a causal effect.

NRC counts word occurrences across eight emotions. Ties use alphabetical order; all tied labels remain visible in review details. No matched emotion words produces “none.” Negation and sarcasm are not modeled by this baseline.

05 / METHOD & EVIDENCE

Method and sources

REQUESTS

No shared conversation

Binary and three-class runs use separate prompts. Each request contains a system prompt plus one review’s title and text. No earlier answers or examples from the other run are included.

INPUT FIELDS

Rating exclusion

Rating metadata never enters the model request. Explicit star-rating phrases in the title and body are masked. The original text, masked input, and model response are preserved for auditing.

REPRODUCIBILITY

Fixed samples, saved responses

Lexicon source and terms

Class-level evidence

Precision = correct among predicted; recall = correct among actual. F1 balances both.

Read the exact classification prompt
Inspect run settings and limitations
Star ratings are the evaluation benchmark, not independently annotated textual sentiment. A mismatch can reflect a classifier error, a text–rating inconsistency, or an ambiguous review. These two runs change both sampling and the label scheme, so differences cannot be attributed to balancing alone. Rating masking is a transparent regex heuristic, not a guarantee that every implicit rating clue is removed.
Temperature 0 and a fixed request seed improve repeatability; the shared inference server may still vary. Saved responses are the authoritative snapshot. The LLM emotion is generated in the same request as sentiment; NRC scoring is independent and receives neither LLM output nor rating metadata.
